summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Research design and 22 source leads on startups and digital government. Q1: startup barrier register designed (entry, foreign capital under FITTA, inbound and outbound foreign payments, startup support, de facto constraints), with de jure rules from primary texts (Law Commission, NRB, DoInd/OCR) and de facto evidence from World Bank Enterprise Surveys/B-READY. Q2: 'fully online' defined as end-to-end transactional; a ten-service inventory and index series (UN EGDI/OSI, World Bank GTMI) are set up, with uptake to come only from administrative counts. Q3: cross-border digital payment constraints mapped by flow (inbound export receipts, outbound digital purchases, international wallets, QR interoperability, India-side RBI rules). Many URLs are home pages from general knowledge (unverified). No values retrieved; all empirical items pending.

findings.claim: Barrier register design for Q1: each barrier recorded with (instrument, issuing authority, date, requirement, who it binds, evidence type). Categories: entry (company/industry registration, minimum capital, PAN/VAT), foreign capital (FITTA minimum amount, approval route, repatriation), foreign payments inbound (receiving export proceeds, platform/wallet access) and outbound (paying for cloud, software, ads, SaaS; card limits), and IP/contract enforcement. De jure rules from primary texts; de facto time/cost from Enterprise Surveys/B-READY.

'Fully online' definition for Q2: a service is fully online only if application, identity verification, payment and delivery of the output can be completed without an office visit (transactional stage in UN DESA OSI terms). Information-only or downloadable-form services are recorded separately. Uptake = transactions or active users per period from administrative data; index scores (EGDI, GTMI) are not uptake measures.

Q3 scope: cross-border digital payments include (a) inbound receipts for services exported by firms/freelancers, (b) outbound payments by residents for digital services, (c) consumer cross-border QR/wallet payments. Rules are recorded from NRB FX and payment-system directives and the Foreign Exchange (Regulation) Act; India-side rules (RBI) recorded separately.
Q1: annual company registrations (total, private companies, foreign-invested) and registered IT/service industries.
